#4471 review: two distinct date problems

owner Mark Young and Codex investigated reviewed 2026-10-28 · 0 days ago

The exported incident says “one issue, one fix queued.” Its rendered views disagree: two mechanisms share one ticket. Five report bodies include timing observations that the classification does not explain; these remain caveats, not demonstrated additional causes. A queued parser fix does not establish that either other problem is fixed.

Scope and evidence

This review uses the October 4 export, not a live support queue. Deduplicate by report ID before counting. Tenant locale and booking form determine the date path; browser locale and intake tags are guesses. The source functions live in src/lib/kb/causes.ts, the directory in src/lib/data/tenants/, and exceptional report IDs in src/lib/data/desk-notes.json.

5 reports read as a one-day move; filed under parser by tenant.

The existing classifier assigns five reports flagged by the desk as one-day moves to parser by tenant and channel. The accepted tickets cover 379 parser reports and 33 hint reports, without overlap. These five reports are included in 379; a count is not proof that the parser caused every symptom. Preserve the original bodies and verify them during investigation.

Separate fixes and verification

  • Shared parser: parse the tenant’s date format consistently. A day-first date such as 07/04 must mean 7 April, not July 4. Test app, email, and booking-v2 form paths; verify the full day-first tenant directory.
  • booking-v3 hint: display the date order expected by its locale-aware form parser. Its MM/DD/YYYY hint induces month-first input in day-first tenants. Test Alder Physio, Copper Studio, and Pale Harbour. Fixing the shared parser alone leaves this path wrong.
  • Timing anomalies: investigate the four one-day report bodies independently. A timezone or date-only conversion is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated cause. Reproduce Lisbon/Toronto display and invite-versus-calendar day differences; inspect original payloads, zones, and event timestamps. R-41236 reports an invite preceding its booking and also needs event-order evidence. These observations remain attached to the parser group pending evidence; no extra cause is asserted.

Received is not merged

The problem was reported in April. July’s merge spike reflects backlog consolidation. Continue tracking arrivals separately from desk merges, and monitor the unresolved timing reports through the October 4 report; the export cannot establish what happened after that date.

Replace subject-only deduplication

The triage prose and accepted decision 0001 date to June 2024. The runbook flags pages older than 180 days as stale. Meanwhile, the executable explorer already compares causes:

Different subjects can describe the same cause; identical subjects can hide different paths. Merge only after checking tenant, channel, form, locale, and symptoms. Unknown tenants and timing anomalies remain unclassified pending investigation. Preserve accepted decision 0001 as history; a new decision should supersede it rather than rewrite it. The explorer is useful evidence, but its classifier still misses the timing reports.
